text: {"memo": "Johnson & Johnson delivered FY2024 revenue of $88.82\u202fbillion, up from $85.16\u202fbillion in FY2023, representing a modest growth rate. Net income fell sharply to $14.07\u202fbillion in FY2024 from $35.15\u202fbillion a year earlier, compressing the net margin. Diluted EPS declined to $5.79 in FY2024 versus $13.72 in FY2023. Operating cash flow improved to $24.27\u202fbillion in FY2024 from $22.79\u202fbillion in FY2023, supporting continued dividend capacity. The operating cash flow margin rose to about 27% in FY2024 from roughly 27% in FY2023, indicating robust cash conversion despite lower profitability. The strong cash generation has allowed JNJ to maintain its dividend and retain flexibility for strategic investments. However, the sharp drop in net income and EPS signals pressure on earnings, which may affect valuation multiples. Investors should monitor cost controls and the ability to restore earnings growth. View: JNJ trades at a premium to its recent cash flow generation and warrants a cautious stance."}
